new_statements.quote: Relevant features of the language: Three tones: H, M, L; not much interaction between tones, and tones are not that complex from a nominal morphology perspective. Not much morphology. No extensive gender system.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File (11 pp., text layer, Author metadata 'Jakob Lesage', created 2023-09-15) opened with extracted text. On p.2, section 0 'Pre-amble', the bullet 'Relevant features of the language' is followed by sub-bullets: 'Three tones: H, M, L; not much interaction between tones, and tones are not that complex from a nominal morphology perspective.' / 'Not much morphology. No extensive gender system.' / 'Modifiers always follow the noun.'... The report's quote is these words exactly; the only differences are that the bullet structure is flattened into running text and a colon is inserted after 'Relevant features of the language' (no colon in the original). A full-document grep for stress/accent/promi…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Baa is described as a tone language with three level tones (High, Mid, Low), with floating L tones and downstep in possessive constructions; the accessible first-hand materials (this handout, the 2020 dictionary whose every entry is tone-marked H/M/L with vowel length) make no statement about word stress or accent at all.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the handout adds (pp. 6-7) that alienable possession involves vowel lengthening plus a floating L tone realized as HL contour or downstep - tonal, not accentual, facts.
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical tone on nouns/words; no word- or phrase-level stress domain is discussed. The fuller 2018 grammar sketch (181 pp., ELAR, login-gated) presumably has a phonology chapter that would settle whether any stress/accent is posited.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources describe Baa = Kwah/Kwa [kwb], kwaa1262, spoken in Kwah and Gyakan villages (Lamurde/Numan LGA, Adamawa State); Glottolog lists two dialects, Gyakan [gyak1238] and Nuclear Kwa [nucl1372], said to 'differ mainly in phonology' (Kleinewillinghöfer 2011). Möller Nwadigo's data were collected mostly from Kwah-village speakers resident in Lagos plus recordings made in the home area; the dictionary is titled Kwah-English. Not to be confused with the Kwa branch of Niger-Congo (Ghana/Côte d'Ivoire/Togo) - Glottolog ref 98925 ('Languages of the Akan area... Western Kwa') attached to kwaa1262 is a mis-assignment.
